rows.question: Which company built the spacecraft Michael Collins stayed in while the first Moon landing took place?
rows.answer:
Michael Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)". Columbia was the Apollo 11 command module of the command and service module [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Apollo 11's command module was Columbia (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)". That module was built by North American Aviation [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Built by North American Aviation (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". North American Aviation was the prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module [[north-american-aviation]] "[stated] Prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

**Answer: North American Aviation.**

rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
Before launch, the tank's heaters were run on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours to empty the tank. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The Apollo 13 Review Board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The board's report also called the switch failure a serious oversight that all parties share. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

The brain does not give a range for the heater run, so "about eight hours" is the only figure stated.

rows.question: How long before Kennedy's speech at Rice University did NASA announce its Apollo mission mode?
rows.answer:
NASA announced lunar orbit rendezvous as the Apollo mission mode on 1962-07-11 [[lunar-orbit-rendezvous]] "- [stated] NASA announced it as the Apollo mission mode on 1962-07-11 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". Kennedy gave the "We choose to go to the Moon" speech at Rice University on 1962-09-12 [[john-f-kennedy]] "- [stated] Gave the 'We choose to go to the Moon' speech at Rice University on 1962-09-12 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

The announcement came 63 days before the Rice speech, about nine weeks. This is my own count from the two dates, not a figure stated in the notes.

The brain gives only the year, 1966. The month and day of the flight are not in it.

rows.question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?
rows.answer:
The astronaut who caught German measles was Charlie Duke, the backup lunar module pilot. He [[charlie-duke]] "[stated] Caught German measles from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". His exposure set off the crew swap that removed Ken Mattingly and put Jack Swigert on the flight [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Backup lunar module pilot Charlie Duke caught German measles and exposed the crews (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)".

The office Swigert later won was a seat in the US House of Representatives. He [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)". So he won the 1982 House election, but he died before taking office.

rows.question: The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was carried by a spacecraft. Which Apollo 11 crew member piloted that kind of spacecraft, and what did he do during the landing?
rows.answer:
The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was oxygen tank No. 2. The Apollo 13 tank "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)" [[oxygen-tank-2]]. The service module carried that tank: "[stated] Its service module carried the oxygen tanks that supplied power and air (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)" [[command-service-module]].

Michael Collins piloted that spacecraft on Apollo 11. He was "[stated] Command module pilot of Apollo 11 (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)" [[michael-collins]]. The command and service module is also linked as piloted by him [[command-service-module]].

During the landing, he stayed in lunar orbit. "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)" [[michael-collins]].

rows.question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?
rows.answer:

[[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] Engineers devised an adapter from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The crew built it from radioed instructions. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The crew built it from radioed instructions (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The adapter was designed at Mission Control Houston. [[mission-control-houston]] "[stated] Engineers there devised the Apollo 13 carbon dioxide scrubber adapter (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The notes do not give the step-by-step build procedure or what the radioed instructions said.

rows.question: How did the Cortright report describe the switch failure?
rows.answer:
The Cortright report, the Report of the Apollo 13 Review Board that Edgar Cortright signed, called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

It also recommended removing all electrical equipment from inside the oxygen tank pressure vessel. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Recommended removing all electrical equipment from inside the oxygen tank pressure vessel (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

The board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The switches themselves were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC, and the heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts without the switches being changed. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Its thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)" [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The opened notes do not contain the report's own wording on the switch failure, so the first three points come from secondary coverage and summaries.

rows.question: Which companies and laboratories built Apollo hardware in the brain, and what did each build?
rows.answer:
Four companies and laboratories are recorded as building Apollo hardware:

- **North American Aviation** was the prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module. [[north-american-aviation]] "[stated] Prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". The command and service module note also says it was built by North American Aviation: [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Built by North American Aviation (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

- **Grumman** built the Apollo lunar module. [[grumman]] "[stated] Built the Apollo lunar module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". The lunar module note agrees: [[lunar-module]] "[stated] Two-stage lander built by Grumman (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

- **MIT Instrumentation Laboratory** designed the Apollo guidance and navigation system. [[mit-instrumentation-lab]] "[stated] Designed the Apollo guidance and navigation system (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". Its on-board computer is the Apollo Guidance Computer, which the computer note says was designed there: [[apollo-guidance-computer]] "[stated] Designed at the MIT Instrumentation Laboratory (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

- **Beech Aircraft** was a North American subcontractor that built the service module oxygen tanks. [[beech-aircraft]] "[stated] Built the service module oxygen tanks under North American Aviation (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)".

I left out two claims I could not cite word for word. The Apollo 1 note links North American as its builder, but its fact lines describe the 1967 cabin fire and do not say what hardware was built. The oxygen tank No. 2 note links Beech Aircraft as its builder, but its fact lines do not state that, so I have not used it.

rows.question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
rows.answer:
Apollo 13 in 1970, in date order:

- **1970-04-06:** Blood tests from the physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"
- **1970-04-10:** The crew swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference. Jack Swigert replaced Mattingly as command module pilot. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"; [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"
- **1970-04-11:** Apollo 13 launched. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **1970-04-13:** Oxygen tank No. 2 exploded, about 56 hours into the flight. The same day, a Mission Control abort decision changed the goal from a Fra Mauro landing to a safe return to Earth. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"; [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **1970-04-17:** The crew, using the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat, splashed down. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **June 1970:** The Cortright Apollo 13 Review Board published its report, which traced the explosion to the tank No. 2 switches. The brain gives only the month. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"
